source.title: Task-dependent clustering in permutation-aligned neural network weights
source.authors: Patrick Krauss; Achim Schilling; Andreas K. Maier; T. Kinfe; Henrik Stubner; Niklas Römmelt; C. Metzner

record.tranche_reason: Tests convergence across independent initializations using aligned-weight dissimilarities and representation similarity, and checks whether the result changes across measures and a function-preserving scaling transformation. It does not test convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on independently trained networks, aligned weights, hidden representations, task changes, and alternative similarity measures. Accuracy and weight-displacement values are included only where they contextualize the reported early emergence of structure. Cited results from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Independently initialized 784→64→10 MLPs are compared within and between datasets and tasks, using aligned weights, CKA and matched-neuron activation correlations. This bears directly on V3 (seed convergence), V6 (measure, gauge and alignment dependence) and V7 (incomplete alignment driven by shared data and objective). It uses a different method from the convergent-learning original. There is no scale, cross-modal, mapping or feature-universality test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The record omits that the authors attribute the clustering to shared inputs and objectives, without forcing a single weight configuration. They also note the separation survives the stronger Git Re-Basin matching, and that differentiation coincides with early functional learning rather than following it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses small shallow image-classification MLPs, permutation-aware weight comparisons, CKA, and controlled task changes; it does not test the scale/performance or cross-modal convergence proposed by the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. It also differs from the original convergent-learning representation studies in its emphasis on aligned weights and training trajectories.
record.method_sensitivity: Raw Alpha changed under function-preserving ReLU rescaling; different measures shifted effect magnitudes and layer contributions; Alpha and CKA agreed on group separation but not reliably on between-dataset pair rankings; PIF-Hungarian and Git Re-Basin yielded different neuron correspondences and different alignment strength.
record.problems: Evidence is limited to small, one-hidden-layer MLPs and three low-resolution grayscale classification datasets, with a single principal SGD configuration. No model-size or capability sweep, cross-modal comparison, or out-of-distribution probe test was performed. Raw Alpha depends on a gauge choice; alignment methods yield different correspondences. The study does not measure attractor basins or recovery after perturbation.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for final accuracies, displacement-from-initialization values, alignment assignment agreement, or pairwise counts: these are contextual, not direct measures of the convergence versions. Supplementary analyses are described but their individual numerical outcomes are not included here unless stated in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; architecture, objective and data are not varied with scale.
No vision–language or paired image–caption comparison.
Only one-hidden-layer MLPs of width 64 with one SGD configuration; no deep networks or widths.
No linear mapping, stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping tests.
No interpretable features, circuits or SAE features identified across models.
No neighbour-count settings and no out-of-distribution probe sets.
No test of whether a common model of reality contributes; no other model families.

missing.what: Initialization baseline for canonical layer-balanced Alpha: within 0.2688, between 0.2691, contrast 0.0003 (CI includes zero). This is the direct convergence baseline for V3.
Matched raw W0 Alpha within 0.0641 and between 0.3579, contrast 0.2938 (0.2901–0.2975), at E=20.
Canonical Alpha by alignment method: PIF-Hungarian within 0.0789 and between 0.3015; Git Re-Basin within 0.0409 and between 0.1985. Pooled: unaligned 0.4780, PIF 0.2324, Git Re-Basin 0.1496.

record.verdict_notes: Small single-hidden-layer MLPs on MNIST-family data only. Many within- versus between-dataset contrasts use between-dataset pairs as the control rather than initialization. The V3 seed-convergence evidence comes from within-group values against initialization and unaligned baselines. R19 duplicates R1.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no test of convergence across models differing in architecture, modality, or training data as scale increases.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language model comparison.
Only small, one-hidden-layer MLPs with the same architecture and training setup are studied for the main independent-seed comparisons; no deep or varied architecture comparison.

No test of mapping one model's representation to another with a linear map, stitching, relative representations, or without paired data. Neuron matching is used to compare units, not to test interchangeability by those methods.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits, neurons, or SAE features are identified or tested.
Tests several dissimilarities, CKA, a ReLU-rescaling transformation, and alignment choices. Does not test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution probe inputs.

Tests clustering and task dependence in the stated small MLP experiments, but not whether shared data or objectives explain alignment in other model families or whether a common model of reality contributes.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (10 MNIST, 10 Fashion-MNIST, 10 KMNIST runs; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared canonically gauged, layer-balanced Alpha dissimilarity after direct canonical-Alpha profile Hungarian alignment.
rows.note: Aggregate over 135 within-dataset and 300 between-dataset pairs; uncertainty estimated by deleting complete runs, not individual pairs. Nonzero within-dataset dissimilarity means the networks did not converge to one parameter point.
rows.check: Link is fine. For V3, the more direct baseline is initialization (within 0.2688, between 0.2691), which no row records. Between-dataset is a control, not the convergence baseline.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated matched W0 Alpha and hidden 1−CKA pair values.
rows.note: The pooled association reflects the two distinct within- and between-dataset groups; it does not establish that the measures rank all pairs similarly.
rows.check: This is the agreement between two measures, not a convergence measure; drop V3 and V7. The authors say the group separation inflates the pooled r, so it cannot show agreement between the measures.

rows.operation_detail: Correlated matched W0 Alpha and hidden 1−CKA pair values.
rows.note: The measures have a positive but less-than-pooled association for within-dataset pair rankings.
rows.check: This is a measure-agreement statistic, not seed convergence; drop V3. It shows moderate within-group agreement between Alpha and CKA.

rows.operation_detail: Correlated matched W0 Alpha and hidden 1−CKA pair values.
rows.note: The confidence interval includes zero; the measures' pairwise rankings did not reliably track each other in this group.
rows.check: Drop V3. Relative to V6, the measure dependence appears: Alpha and CKA do not agree on the ranking of between-dataset pairs. So the state is observed, not absent.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked canonical, layer-balanced Alpha for within- and between-dataset pairs.
rows.note: The separation appeared by the first half-epoch checkpoint and was described as stable across the sampled trajectory.
rows.check: The V7 link fits because within-dataset dissimilarity plateaus at about 0.077–0.079 from E=1 to E=20 and stays nonzero.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Repeated raw Alpha analysis after function-preserving positive neuronwise ReLU rescaling.
rows.note: The contrast fell to about 65% of its original size but remained positive. Network predictions were unchanged; largest absolute logit difference was below 5 × 10⁻14.
rows.check: The study's raw Alpha contrast shrinks to 65% under a function-preserving rescaling, but does not vanish. Drop V3 and V7.

source_check.correct: V6 state: observed. Function-preserving rescaling reduces raw Alpha contrast from 0.1559 to 0.1008, approximately 65% of its original magnitude; the contrast remains positive.
source_check.problem: V6 predicts weakening or disappearance; the observed weakening satisfies that prediction without requiring disappearance.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed Alpha after canonicalizing each hidden neuron's incoming and outgoing weight norms.
rows.note: Canonicalization removed the tested positive neuronwise rescaling freedom and preserved the principal dataset separation.
rows.check: This duplicates R1's value. Under the canonical gauge the contrast is unaffected by rescaling, so for V6 no dependence remains. Drop V3 and V7.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean correlation of activations for matched hidden neurons.
rows.note: Every one of the 135 within-dataset pairs improved over the unaligned order; the mean correlation remained below 1.
rows.check: For V3, V3 itself predicts partial unit correspondence (0.31, against 0.07 unaligned), so this is observed rather than partial. It also bears on V7 (correspondence far from complete) and on V6 (depends on alignment method; compare R22).

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean correlation of activations for matched hidden neurons.
rows.note: The increase was small; PIF-Hungarian improved 69.7% of between-dataset pairs.
rows.check: These are between-dataset pairs, so not V3. Networks trained on different data have almost no unit correspondence (0.052).

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean correlation of activations for matched hidden neurons.
rows.note: Git Re-Basin outperformed PIF-Hungarian, but the correspondence was not complete.
rows.check: Git Re-Basin is an external baseline rather than the study's own method. It is still valid as evidence of alignment-method dependence (0.49 against 0.31).

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean correlation of activations for matched hidden neurons.
rows.note: Git Re-Basin outperformed PIF-Hungarian, but between-dataset correspondence remained far from complete.

rows.subject: 30-network cohort (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared raw weight cosine similarity across alignment conditions.

conditions.value: unaligned versus PIF-Hungarian versus Git Re-Basin

rows.note: Aggregate comparison over all pairs; Git Re-Basin's objective directly increases weight inner product.
rows.check: This is largely a comparison of alignment methods, pooled over within- and between-dataset pairs, and Git Re-Basin directly optimizes this quantity. It cannot show V3. At most it shows alignment-method dependence.

relationships.condition: Independent seeds of the same MLP trained on the same dataset or task
relationships.reason: Within-group pairs are more similar than between-group pairs in aligned weights and in CKA (R1–R8, R12, R13). This structure appears within a few updates (R15–R17). Matched units correlate only partially (R20, R22), consistent with shared features but not identical units.
relationships.display_finding: Aligned weights and CKA grouped networks by dataset or task within a few updates, while matched units correlated only partially.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Independent seeds of the same MLP trained on the same dataset or task
source_check.reason: Within-dataset dissimilarity decreases from initialization, within-group weights and representations become more similar than between-group comparisons, and matched neurons show partial correspondence.

relationships.condition: Effect magnitudes, layer attribution, pairwise rankings and unit correspondence
relationships.reason: Raw Alpha contrast falls to 65% under function-preserving rescaling (R18). The layer carrying the effect flips between measures (R2–R7). Alpha and CKA disagree on between-dataset pair rankings (R11). Unit correspondence depends on the alignment method (R20 vs R22, R24).
relationships.display_finding: Function-preserving rescaling reduced the raw Alpha contrast to 65%, measures assigned the effect to different layers, Alpha and CKA disagreed on between-dataset pair rankings, and alignment methods changed unit correspondence.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Effect magnitudes, layer attribution, pairwise rankings and unit correspondence
source_check.reason: Rescaling changes raw Alpha contrast; measures assign different layer magnitudes and disagree on between-dataset pairwise detail; alignment methods yield different unit correspondence.

relationships.condition: Direction of the broad within- vs between-group separation
relationships.reason: The grouping does not vanish under any tested measure (canonical Alpha, Euclidean, SND, CKA) or under the canonical gauge (R4–R8, R19). So V6's 'weakens or vanishes' holds for magnitudes, not for the direction.
relationships.display_finding: Within-group versus between-group separation persisted under canonical Alpha, Euclidean, SND, and CKA measures and under the canonical gauge.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Direction of the broad within- vs between-group separation
source_check.reason: Broad grouping persists across the tested measures and canonicalization, qualifying any interpretation that measurement dependence necessarily removes the group structure.

relationships.condition: Same-architecture MLPs with shared versus differing data or objective
relationships.reason: Within-group dissimilarity stays nonzero and plateaus (R1, R17), and matched-unit correlations stay far below 1 (R20, R22). Networks on different datasets barely correspond (R21, R23). Changing only the objective on identical images and initial weights separates the networks (R12–R14).
relationships.display_finding: Within-group dissimilarity plateaued above zero and matched-unit correlations stayed far below 1; changing datasets nearly eliminated correspondence, while changing objectives separated networks despite identical images and initial weights.

relation.reason: The study directly measures seed convergence, measurement dependence and the contribution of shared training constraints.

tranche.reason: Controlled comparisons of independently initialized networks test shared internal structure through permutation-aligned weights, CKA and activation correspondence.

source_check.notes: Identity and parity use 10 versus 2 output logits; the task control compares W0 and hidden representations, and Git Re-Basin robustness was established only for the main dataset cohort. Rescaling statements are supported by R18 rather than their cited R1/R8; no scale, cross-modal, exclusive-cause or attractor conclusion is established.

statements.correction: Study-specific label: limits_scope. Dataset grouping persists under canonical Alpha, Euclidean, SND and CKA; raw Alpha contrast weakens under rescaling; layer attribution and pairwise agreement depend on the measure.
statements.problem: The robustness claim is correct, but challenges overstates its implication for V6: grouping persists while magnitudes, layer attribution and pairwise correspondence remain measure-dependent.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Independent runs of the same 784→64→10 MLP trained on the same dataset; aligned weights and hidden representations
reader_labels.reason: Within-dataset pairs were more similar than between-dataset pairs (R1–R8), and matched-neuron activation correlations improved over unaligned numbering (R20, R22). The evidence supports shared, task-related structure, not identity of units or parameters.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Extent and nature of convergence in the tested models
reader_labels.reason: Within-dataset dissimilarity remained nonzero, and matched-unit correlations were incomplete; the authors describe clustering rather than convergence to a common point (R1, R20, R22).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Raw Alpha under function-preserving ReLU rescaling; fine-grained comparison of Alpha and CKA
reader_labels.reason: Rescaling changed the Alpha contrast from 0.1559 to 0.1008, and Alpha–CKA pairwise association fell to r=0.1071 for between-dataset pairs (R11, R18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Broad within-versus-between grouping across tested measures and canonical gauge
reader_labels.reason: The direction of the dataset separation remained positive with canonical Alpha, Euclidean dissimilarity, SND, and CKA; canonicalization retained the principal contrast (R1–R8, R19). Thus the broad grouping did not vanish under these tested alternatives.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Dataset-defined clusters in the main cohort and objective change on fixed MNIST inputs
reader_labels.reason: Same-dataset pairs were closer than different-dataset pairs, with nonzero within-dataset distance; changing identity to parity while holding images fixed also separated weights and representations (R1, R12–R14).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Early training and metric/alignment qualifications in the tested MLPs
reader_labels.reason: The group separation appeared early and persisted across sampled training; alternative measures retained it, while ReLU rescaling altered raw Alpha's magnitude and matched-unit correspondence remained incomplete (R15–R19, R20–R24).
